'''Rachel "Raya" Takserman-Krozer''' (31 December 1921 – 28 September 1987) was a theoretical physicist and professor of [[rheology]]. Takserman-Krozer worked on diverse aspects of theoretical physics ranging from [[theory of relativity]] to studies of [[polymer]]s and their flow. Her scientific work includes contributions to behaviour of [[polymers]] and polymers solutions in velocity fields, theory of spinnability, problems of phenomenological [[rheology]], and molecular-statistical theory of polymer networks. Takserman-Krozer worked across several countries including Russia, Poland, Israel, and Germany.

She received the Polish Chemical Society Scientific Award in 1963, and was listed in Who's who in Israel 1972<ref name="WswIsrael">{{cite book|url=http://www.ha-mafteah.org/wwi/|title=Who's who in Israel and in the work for Israel abroad|publisher=Tel Aviv : Bronfman & Cohen Publishers, Ltd.|year=1972|edition=15th biannual printing}}</ref> and the International Register of Profiles of the [[International Biographical Centre]]

== Biography ==
Rachel (Raya) Takserman-Krozer was born on 31 December 1921 in [[Haisyn]], [[Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic|Ukrainian SSR]] into a Jewish family. After moving to [[Odesa]], Takserman-Krozer finished her school education and was admitted to the Faculty of Physics at the University of Odessa. During the Second World War she volunteered as a nurse and continued her study of physics at the university of [[Tashkent]], [[Uzbekistan]], where she obtained an MSc degree in Theoretical Physics in 1945. She married Szymon (Simon) Krozer in 1946, who studied [[experimental physics]] at the university of [[Tashkent]] and later became professor of experimental polymer physics. In 1948 she started her doctoral studies on theory of relativity with [[V. A. Fock]] at the Institute of Theoretical Physics in Leningrad University now St. Petersburg State University.<ref name="V. A. Fock Institute">{{citation|title=V. A. Fock Institute|url=http://www.niif.spbu.ru/en/|access-date=2016-01-02|archive-date=2009-10-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091016081542/http://www.niif.spbu.ru/en/|url-status=dead}}</ref> During this time she lectured at the [[Petrozavodsk State University]].<ref name="Petrozavodsk State University">{{citation|title=St. Petersburg State University|url=http://petrsu.ru/Structure/structure_e.htm}}</ref> During this time she gave birth to three sons: Anatol Krozer<ref name="Anatol Krozer">{{citation|title=Anatol Krozer|url=https://www.acreo.se/people/anatol-krozer}}</ref> in 1949, who became a surface science physicist focusing on development of bio- and chemical sensors at [[ACREO]], [[Research Institutes of Sweden (RISE)]], [[Gothenburg]], Sweden, Georgij (Yoram) Krozer<ref name="Yoram Krozer">{{citation|title=Yoram Krozer|url=https://www.utwente.nl/bms/cstm/people/senior-staff/krozer/}}</ref> in 1953, who studied biology and economics and works as an associated professor on innovations for sustainable development at the [[University of Twente]], Netherlands, and Viktor Krozer<ref name="Viktor Krozer">{{citation|title=Viktor Krozer|url=http://www.uni-frankfurt.de/47597593/Viktor-Krozer}}</ref> in 1958, who studied electrical engineering and is now professor of Terahertz Photonics and Electronics at faculty of physics at the [[Goethe University Frankfurt]], Germany.

In 1959 she resumed her PhD studies at the Laboratory of Polymer Physics of the Industrial Chemistry Institute, headed by Andrzej Ziabicki.  She completed her PhD ([[Warsaw]], 1962) and habilitation ([[Łódź]], 1966), both in polymer physics. In 1967 and 1968 she worked in the Institute of Fundamental Technological Research, Polish Academy of Sciences, Warsaw, Poland on hydrodynamics and rheology of polymer solutions and suspensions, "spinnability of liquids", extensional flows and problems related to the theory of polymer processing.

In August 1968 she obtained a position as a professor at the Department of Mechanics at the [[Israel Institute of Technology]] ([[Technion]]) headed, at that time, by [[Marcus Reiner]], the founder of Rheology, where she worked on the subjects of Microrheology and Nonlinear Rheology.

In 1972, she continued her research at the [[RWTH Aachen University]], [[University of Karlsruhe]] and finally at the [[University of Stuttgart]], working together with [[Ekkehart Kröner]]. She deceased in [[Trier]], Germany, after three years of fight against lung cancer, on 28 September 1987. According to her last wish, she had been entombed in [[Amsterdam]], Netherlands.

== Scientific work ==
Taksmeran-Krozer's main contributions are in the field of Polymer Physics and Rheology. She has made substantial contributions to the field of rheology together with [[Marcus Reiner]] and to the field of behaviour of polymer solutions and networks. Her research work has been published predominantly in the ''[[Journal of Polymer Science]]'', the Bulletin de L’Académie  Polonaise des Sciences, Rheologica Acta,<ref name="Rheologica Acta">{{citation|title=Rheologica Acta|url=http://link.springer.com/journal/397}}</ref> and [[Colloid and Polymer Science]].

=== Behaviour of polymer solutions in velocity fields ===
Takserman-Krozer focused on various problems related to polymer processing - structure development, rheology, relation between structure and physical properties, contributing to the understanding of elongational (extensional) flow of polymer suspensions and solutions. <!--
Studying fundamentals of fibre spinning it was concluded that the behaviour of 
macromolecules in elongational flow is different to that in shear flow and this 
difference may provide a key factor in understanding polymer processing. 
--> Her solution of the ellipsoid orientation distribution in form of series expansion was later supplemented by an exact solution of a similar problem (orientation in shear flow) by [[Werner Kuhn (chemist)|Werner Kuhn]]. <!--
When asking [[Werner Kuhn (chemist)|Werner Kuhn]] how he obtained his solution, his answer was simply: ”I 
guessed it”.
--> Then Takserman-Krozer and [[Andrzej Ziabicki]] made a systematic study of elongational flow behaviour of various molecular models and rheological behaviour of polymers. <!--
Some of the results were not free from artifacts: applying Cerf ’s assumption about 
rotational part of the  molecular velocity brought about unphysical predictions about 
the stress tensor: antisymmetric components proportional to intramolecular rigidity 
(internal viscosity).
--> <ref>{{cite book|author=W. N. Cwietkow|title=Struktura makroczasteczek w roztworach|author2=W. Je. Eskin|author3=S. Ja. Frenkel|location=Warsaw|publisher=Wydawnictwo Naukowo-Techniczne, 1968.|editor=S. Krozer|editor2=A. Pastusiak|editor3=R. Takserman-Krozer}}</ref>

=== Theory  of spinnability ===
Spinnability of liquids was another problem related to fibre spinning studied in parallel with hydrodynamics and [[rheology]] of polymer solutions and suspensions. <!--
In the thirties, forties and fifties many experimental  papers mentioned 
”spinnability”, but the physical concept was not well defined. Intuitively,  one 
would hardly expect mercury to form anything but drops. So the observation that 
polymers behave differently and can be effectively spun into fibres was counter-
intuitive. At the same  time, people dealing with  highly viscous materials, like  
bitumina, or polyethylene melts, found that high viscosity and rapid deformations are 
the factors preventing the material from being drawn into fibres.  Experimental data 
indicate also that ”spinnability” characterized  as the maximum length of liquid 
threads,  passes through maximum when plotted vs. viscosity of the liquid, or speed 
of elongation.
--> Takserman-Krozer and [[Andrzej Ziabicki]] found factors limiting spinnability, i.e. the maximum length of liquid threads, to obey two mechanisms: development of Rayleigh [[capillary waves]] on the surface of liquid threads and their break-up into drops, and [[brittle fracture]] of viscoelastic threads when the accumulated  elastic energy compensates cohesive forces. <!--
The first mechanism, active at low viscosities and low elongation rates predicts an 
increase of spinnability with [[viscosity]] and [[strain rate]]; the same factors 
stimulate [[fracture]] and reduce spinnability in highly viscoelastic materials. 
Using simple rheology and dynamics of a steady-state fluid jet, Takserman-
Krozer and [[Andrzej Ziabicki]] derived expressions for liquid thread lengths, 
qualitatively  consistent  with empirical data. 
--> Direct observations of capillary break-up and cohesive fracture also spoke in favour of the proposed theory. In spite of later efforts by Takserman-Krozer and coworkers the theory of spinnability never reached the level of a quantitative theory.

=== Phenomenological rheology ===
Takserman Krozer investigated basic problems of phenomenological (classical) rheology and closure of the gap between the micro structure of the materials and their macro mechanical behaviour. In her work with [[Marcus Reiner]], the phenomenological rheology approach of a combination of linear bodies was used for the analysis of the dynamic strength limit of both viscoelastic solid and elastic-viscous liquid. <!--
Based on thermodynamic  parameters such as free volume and activation energy, the 
parametric non-linearity of the particular cases of volume creep and pressure 
relaxation of the material was analyzed. The effects of heat and pressure on flow 
pattern have special importance in many practical cases,  where the rheological 
parameters of the material are very sensitive to thermodynamic changes. 
--> The general formulation of the problem characterizes the rheological stress/strain relationship of a general compressible fluid, the basic hydrodynamic equations of continuity, motion and energy transfer, and the dependence of the rheological and physical parameters of the material on its thermodynamic state.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Takserman-Krozer|first=R.|author2=N. Galili|date=1970|title=Theory of flow of nonlinear viscoelastic fluid with temperature and pressure dependent rheological parameters in cylindrical pipe: I. General formulation|journal=Technical Report, Technion--Israel Institute of Technology, Dept. Of Mechanics|publisher=Technion|volume=TDM 70-11}}</ref>

A perturbation solution for pressure- and temperature-dependent viscosity has shown that pressure and heating effects may result in apparently non-Newtonian behaviour, with a non-uniform pressure gradient and variable velocity profile along the pipe.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Galili|first=N.|author2=R. Takserman-Krozer|author3=Z. Rigbi|date=1975|title=Heat and pressure effects in viscous flow through a pipe. I. General formulation and basic solution|journal=Rheologica Acta|publisher=Springer|volume=14|issue=6|pages=550–567|doi=10.1007/BF01525306|s2cid=93671229}}</ref><!--
A more general approach  to the problem of temperature and pressure dependend viscous 
flow was developed by Takserman-Krozer and her co-workers and the analysis led 
to simple criteria for predicting heat and pressure effects in viscous flow.
-->

=== Molecular-statistical theory  of polymer networks ===
Takserman-Krozer established the dynamical theory of macromolecular (permanent) networks  at the Institute of Theoretical and Applied Physics of the University of Stuttgart with Ekkehart Kröner. The [[Hartree]] self-consistent field approach as a method to take into account many-body forces such as Oseen's hydrodynamic interaction had been considered. She then, together with Ekkehart Kröner, developed the thermodynamics as well as the molecular-statistical theory of so-called temporary polymer networks, both for equilibrium and nonequilibrium. The theory now stands quantitatively. Properties investigated were in particular the [[non-Newtonian fluid]] flow for shear and elongation flow and the stress overshoot maximum after abrupt start of the flow.

== Honours and prizes ==
In 1963, Takserman-Krozer received the Polish Chemical Society Scientific Award. She is listed in the Who's Who in Israel 1972 and in International Register of Profiles of the [[International Biographical Centre]].{{citation needed|date=October 2021}}
